newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends lower, June expiry awaited.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends lower, June expiry awaited.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures ended lower across the board in active dealings, taking heating oil and unleaded gasoline down as well as the markets consolidated sharp gains posted last week, traders said.

July crude dropped 28 cents to settle at $21.90 a barrel, traded between $22.15 and $21.81. June unleaded gas fell 0.66 cent to 65.21 a gallon, while heating oil futures lost 0.55, closing at 57.92 a gallon.
The expiration of the June crude contract led trading in the complex, traders said, noting little fundamental news to thwart the inevitable profit taking after Friday's rally.
June liquidation, rollovers into July and outer months and considerable crack spread short covering amounted to a day's worth of housecleaning ahead of the expiry, traders said.
"Some refiners came in, the products were relatively stronger than crude today, so there was buying of product and selling of crude," one trader said.
Traders were on the fence about Tuesday's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute, but most said it was unlikely that the market would ignore another week of bearish supply data.
Tuesday's API report will be followed by the U.S. Department of Energy's numbers Wednesday morning.

Markets were also attuned to possible developments on Iraqi and Burmese sanctions. The U.N. sanctions panel was to meet Tuesday afternoon, continuing a process to review implementation of the oil-for-food accord, which comes up for renewal in early June.

The White House was expected to announce sanctions regulations Tuesday against Burma, following a directive by President Bill Clinton last month which seeks to punish the Burmese military government for human rights abuses.
Although Burmese sanctions were not expected to sway prices, U.S. oil majors were watching to see if the move would have an effect on investments in the country.

"It's been really sort of a tough last couple of weeks because there hasn't been a lot of news out. Even though (the complex) was weak today, it's not as if anyone can say that we've topped out. I just see it as nothing definitive," the trader said.
Another trader said cash WTI kept a lot of interest while the June expiry proceeds. "We've got to get rid of this lack of liquidity in June right now," he said.
